authors: R. K. Stoessell, P. A. Byrne
title: Salting-out of methane in single-salt solutions at 25 C and below 800 psia
experimental_method: Titanium-lined saturation chamber rocked 3 h at 25 C and set methane pressure; liquid sample flashed in a sample loop and released gas measured on a mercury manometer; moles from ideal gas law, molar converted to molal with solution densities.
uncertainties_stated: Precision within 0.0005 molal, average 0.0003; pressure gauge within 1 psia; distilled-water values differ by +0.0002 to +0.0014 molal from estimates of their Eqn (3); agreement with Culberson and McKetta (1951) smoothed values -0.0002 to +0.0006 molal.
quality_remarks: Bicarbonate (HCO3) solutions required CO2 corrections and are less accurate; carbonate salts are outside the six-ion set. Seawater row is from the authors' earlier paper (footnote **), not a new measurement in this paper. Table 2 (salting-out constants) is derived.
